memory_rule: The tagger's batches are 250 random sentences, and Stanza pads every sentence of a batch to the longest one before the transformer, so finetuning XLM-R-large in fp32 keeps activations for 250 x (longest sentence in subwords) positions. The smoke test used 43.8 GB on a 46 GB GPU at about 18,000 positions (about 2.4 MB per position). With batch 250 the median batch has 41,250 positions in zh_gsdsimp, 21,750 in de_hdt and 18,125 in tr_imst, beyond an L40S's 44 GiB. Batch 32 bounds a batch at 32 x 512 = 16,384 positions, since Stanza drops training sentences over the 512-subword window, so it fits every registered treebank. Decided from memory alone, before any pilot training, and applied to every treebank. The parser keeps Stanza's 5,000-word batches, which are sorted by length (little padding, about 7,000 to 11,000 positions).
encoder_path_rule: Every job reaches the encoder at /tmp/intract_tp/xlm-roberta-large-c23d21b0, a node-local copy of the pinned snapshot verified by the SHA-256 of model.safetensors (tp_stage_local.sh), so the trained models record that path as bert_model; any later use of X stages the same path.
tokenisation_rule: X takes the registered Stanza 1.15.0 tokenize and mwt output (the <tb>_nocharlm tokenizer and the <tb> mwt package, with gold sentence boundaries in the benchmark) and adds its own UPOS, XPOS, features, heads and relations; lemmas come from the registered <tb>_nocharlm lemmatizer applied to X's tags. X therefore adds no tokenisation error of its own and shares the Stanza member's. Under the long-unit rule a unit over 100 words takes Stanza's parse in every member of the mean. The three-member mean is the unweighted mean of P, U and X.
retag_rule: Depparse is trained on train/dev/test files whose UPOS, XPOS and features were predicted by the treebank's own X POS model (stanza.models.tagger --mode predict --no_pretrain on Stanza's gold depparse copies). Fixed fallback, chosen before any pilot result: gold tags in training.
precision_rule: Training and inference in IEEE fp32 with TF32 off (NVIDIA_TF32_OVERRIDE=0, torch.backends.cuda.matmul.allow_tf32=False). If the projected full training cost exceeds 150 L40S GPU-hours, the recipe changes uniformly (TF32 in training only, or a lower max_steps), decided from timing alone before any full-run benchmark.
stopping_rule: Stanza 1.15.0 defaults: tagger stops after 3,000 steps without a dev AllTags improvement in its second (AMSGrad) stage, switching stage at the first stall; parser switches to Adam at a 2,000-step stall or at step 10,000 and stops after a 2,000-step stall of dev LAS; both stop at max_steps 50,000 at the latest. The best dev checkpoint is the deposited model.

decision_rules.gain: delta rho2 = rho2(P+U+X) - rho2(P+U): the gain in the noise-only gold reliability of the GrammaticalLoad composite C5 (MSL, MDD, CPS, SUB, NPE; anchors from error_model/scripts/gfeat.py) with equal weights on the gold SDs, fixed at the point estimate (tp_bench.py, paired_deltas.PUX_minus_PU_rho2)
decision_rules.interval: paired percentile 95% interval (2.5th and 97.5th percentiles) from the B cluster-bootstrap replicates of each gold condition (documents, or 20-sentence blocks where a file has fewer than 10 documents); every system is scored on the same replicate
decision_rules.averaging: a language's gain is the mean over its available gold conditions, and an average over languages weights each language equally; the bootstrap distribution of an average is the replicate-wise mean of the conditions' replicates (the conditions are resampled independently, so replicates are paired by index)
decision_rules.language_of_condition: the at_risk_languages table, otherwise the ISO prefix of the condition name (de_hdt -> de)

joining_rule_full_benchmark.registered_text: It joins the mean in every language only if, on gold with paired cluster-bootstrap intervals, the lower 95 per cent limit of its gain in the reliability of GrammaticalLoad, averaged over the languages placed at risk under Outcome-neutral quality checks, lies above zero, and the upper limit of the gain lies below zero in no language.
join_if_all: the lower 95% limit of the gain averaged over the at-risk languages (Turkish: IMST and PUD; Simplified Chinese: GSDSimp and PUD; Traditional Chinese: GSD and PUD; Thai: TUD and PUD) is above 0
in no benchmarked language is the upper 95% limit of the language's gain below 0
joining_rule_full_benchmark.evaluable_when: every at-risk language has at least one benchmarked gold condition
joining_rule_full_benchmark.otherwise: X does not join the mean in any language

pilot_go_no_go.applies_to: the pilot: X trained on zh_gsdsimp and tr_imst, benchmarked on zh_gsdsimp, zhs_pud, tr_imst and tr_pud; it decides whether the full 19-treebank training (D(i)) goes ahead
go_if_all: the pilot completes: POS and depparse training completed for both pilot treebanks, and TP-5 benchmarked all four pilot conditions
its determinism checks pass: X and X_rerun byte-identical, and X's sentence count equal to gold, in every pilot condition
the projected full-training cost (tp_project.py, central projection) is at most 150 L40S GPU-hours
the upper 95% limit of the gain averaged over the pilot's at-risk conditions (Simplified Chinese and Turkish, each averaged over its two conditions) is not below 0
